introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.lead: Bibi is a booking system for conferences, food and drink at venues without a hotel system. Your staff use it. Your guests and customers never log in.
introduction.body:
# What Bibi is for

Bibi helps venue staff handle orders from the first contact to the finished event. It is built for places such as experience centres, museums, conference estates, manor houses and restaurants with private rooms.

The people who use it are your sales staff, coordinators, kitchen leads and administrators. Customers and guests never use the app. The only page a customer sees is the payment page you send them.

# What you can do

- **Follow every request in one place.** An order is created as soon as a customer asks, and moves through your own statuses until it is done or lost. See [Orders](/docs/guide/orders).
- **Plan the program.** Add lines to an order, with the room, the setup and the number of people. Rooms cannot be double booked.
- **Record needs as counts.** For example "Gluten x 3" or "Wheelchair x 2", never tied to a named person. See [Needs and run sheets](/docs/guide/needs-and-run-sheets).
- **Send run sheets to the people who need them.** A run sheet is a versioned compilation, for example a kitchen order, and Bibi marks what changed since the last version you sent.
- **Take payment.** Customers pay a link or an invoice, and the money goes straight to your own Stripe account. See [Payments](/docs/guide/payments).
- **Ask the assistant.** You can do most of this by chatting. The assistant proposes changes and you approve them. See [The assistant](/docs/guide/assistant).

# Your organization sets the vocabulary

Bibi does not decide what you call things. Each organization defines its own types, fields, lists, statuses, run sheets and responsibilities. A conference estate may have "Conference room" and "Dish". A museum may have "Gallery" and "Guided tour". This guide uses examples such as allergens and kitchen orders, but they are examples only. What you see in your own account depends on how it is set up. See [Configuration](/docs/guide/configuration).

# Where to start

1. Read [Getting started](/docs/guide/getting-started) to sign in and find your way around.
2. If you are an administrator, set up your types, lists and statuses first.
3. Create an order, either from Orders or by asking the assistant.

# For developers

If you want to connect your own systems, see the [developer documentation](/docs/developers/overview).

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.lead: Sign in, pick your organization and learn where things are in the menu.
getting-started.body:
# Sign in

1. Open Bibi and choose **Sign in**. You can use your password, a **Sign-in link** sent by email, or a **One-time code**.
2. If you are new, choose **Create account**. The password needs at least 10 characters.
3. If a colleague invited you, open the link in the invitation email, sign in with the invited email address and choose **Accept invitation**.

If you belong to several organizations, you land on **Choose organization**. Pick one, or choose **Create organization** to start a new one. You can switch later from the user menu.

# The start page is the assistant

After you sign in you land on a chat. This is the assistant, and it is the quickest way to find things or make a change. Choose **Create chat** to start over. Earlier conversations are listed in the left menu under **Assistant**. See [The assistant](/docs/guide/assistant).

# The left menu

The menu has three parts.

- **Assistant** at the top: the home page, **Create chat** and your recent conversations.
- **Work**: **Orders** and **Customers**.
- **Catalog**: **Items** and **Venues**.

At the bottom left you find **Settings** (only for admins) and your user menu. The user menu holds theme (light, dark or system), language (Swedish or English), switching organization, **My skills** and **Sign out**.

At the top right there is a command bar. Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K on Windows) to search or jump to a page. To the left of it a breadcrumb shows where you are. The assistant lives on the start page.

# A first checklist

If your organization is new and you are an administrator, work through this list. Each step links to a page with details.

1. Create your types under **Settings, Types**, or import a template. See [Configuration](/docs/guide/configuration).
2. Add your lists, for example allergens, under **Settings, Lists**.
3. Review your statuses under **Settings, Statuses**.
4. Create a venue, then add your rooms and other items. See [Items and venues](/docs/guide/items-and-venues).
5. Invite your colleagues under **Settings, Members**. See [Members and roles](/docs/guide/members-and-roles).
6. Connect Stripe under **Settings, Payments** if you want customers to pay online. See [Payments](/docs/guide/payments).
7. Add a customer, then create an order. See [Orders](/docs/guide/orders).

If you are not an administrator, you will not see **Settings**. Ask an administrator in your organization to set up what you need.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.lead: The assistant answers questions and prepares changes for you. It never changes anything until you approve.
assistant.body:
# What it can do

The assistant works as you. It can only see and do what your own role allows, in your own organization. Use it to:

- find orders, customers, items and venues
- show an order, a run sheet or a list of occupied rooms
- prepare a change, for example creating a customer or moving a line

Try questions such as "Show all venues", "Find bookable items that fit 50 people" or "Which skills are available?".

# Where to find it

- On the start page it fills the screen. Choose **Create chat** for a fresh conversation.
- It only lives on the start page. A question asked from the command bar (Cmd+K) takes you there.
- Your recent conversations are listed in the left menu under **Assistant**. You can rename or archive a conversation from its menu.
- On a phone the menu opens as a drawer from the top bar.

# Approving changes

The assistant never saves a change by itself. When it wants to change something it shows an **Approve action** card that lists exactly what will happen.

1. Read the card. Check the fields and values.
2. Choose **Approve** to carry it out, or **Reject** to drop it.
3. A proposal expires after a short time. If you see **The proposal has expired**, ask again.

Every change is recorded in the history of the order or customer. History shows whether the assistant proposed it and who approved it.

# Skills

A skill is a saved set of instructions that the assistant loads when it fits the task, for example "how we write a quote reply". There are three kinds: system skills that come with Bibi, organization skills shared by your administrators, and personal skills only you can see.

- Find organization skills under **Settings, Skills**, and your own under **My skills** in the user menu.
- Choose **Create skill**, describe when it applies and what the assistant should do, then publish it.
- You can also import a SKILL.md file. It arrives as a draft.

# Good to know

- The assistant can be wrong. Check the approval card, not just the chat text.
- It uses the same rules as you do. If you cannot change something, neither can it.
- If the assistant is unavailable, an administrator at Bibi has not selected a model yet. The rest of the app works as usual.
- Developers can connect other tools to the same capabilities. See [MCP](/docs/developers/mcp) and [Approvals](/docs/developers/approvals).

orders.title: Orders
orders.lead: An order is one customer request, from the first contact to the finished event. This page shows how to create one, from who asks to Create, and how to move it through your statuses.
orders.body:
# Create an order

Open **Orders** and choose **Create order**. The page is one screen with steps in order. Only the open step takes input. A finished step collapses to one line with **Change**, which reopens it and keeps the answers after it. Nothing is saved until **Create order**, except a customer or contact you create in step 1.

1. **Who**: search for the customer by name. The five most recent customers show while the box is empty. If the customer is new, choose **New customer** and give the name, type, and a contact name and email. Bibi first checks for a similar customer and says "looks like ..." with **Use ...** or **No, it is a new customer**, so you do not create a duplicate. A contact person is required: the customer's only contact is used, you pick when there are several, and a customer without one asks you to add one.
2. **When and how many**: the date, from and to (in your organization's time zone) and the estimated number of guests.
3. **Package or one-off**: every package is grouped by what is free at that time. **Available** packages fit the time and the guest range. **Not available then** packages clash with another booking. **Outside your time or guest range** packages are made for other guest numbers or run past your end time. Each card shows its guest range and notes such as "Available" or "1 clash with other bookings". **One-off** builds the booking line by line.
4. **Review the booking** (or build it, for a one-off): the lines with their time, quantity and availability, a calendar for the day, notes on the booking, and **Create order**.

# Packages and the follow-up dialog

A package is a ready-made set of lines for a small meeting, with the guest range it is made for. Staff create it once and use it for every similar request. When you pick a package that needs a decision, a dialog asks one question at a time ("question 1 of 3"):

- **Guests outside the range**: lower or raise the booking to the package's range, or keep your number (lines over capacity are flagged).
- **Runs past the requested end**: extend the order, or keep your end and shorten the lines in review.
- **Clashes**: move the booking to the first free time that day, or keep the time and prebook. Prebooked lines are blocked until you move the time or the other booking is freed.

**Cancel, pick another package** leaves nothing picked. If lines already exist and you pick another package, Bibi asks whether to replace the lines or add the new ones. Without any package, the step offers **One-off** and **Create a package**.

# Review, open questions and Create

- **Lines**: **Edit** or **+ Add line** opens the line dialog. Search items of every type or add a free-text line. Set the time, quantity (it follows the guest count until you type a number), setup, choices, price, discount, needs and a note. The dialog shows the availability of the line live. A clash can still be saved: the line is prebooked and shown as blocked.
- **Needs**: counts per value from your lists, for example Vegan 2. See [Needs and run sheets](/docs/guide/needs-and-run-sheets).
- **Open questions**: a yellow panel lists what must be decided before Create, each with its answers, for example "There are no lines. Create the order as a lead without lines?" or a stock shortage. **Create order** says "Answer 2 questions first" until all are answered.
- **One-off**: you can also save the lines as a new package, with a name.
- **More**: assignee (you by default), when holds expire and the estimated value.
- **Create order** makes the order with all its lines at once. When lines clash it says **Create and prebook**. If someone else booked the same thing while you worked, nothing is created: Bibi shows who and when, updates the lines and you check and create again.

The page keeps an unfinished intake in your browser, per organization and member. Next time the first step asks "Continue the draft for ...?" with **Continue** and **Discard**. A created order clears it.

If your organization has an assistant model, you can also start from a message. See [The inbox and starting from a message](/docs/guide/inbox).

# The order page

- **Quotes**: versions of the quote to the customer.
- **Program**: the lines of the order. Choose **Add line** and give a name, time, room, setup and quantity. A room is held for that time, and the setup's changeover time is blocked right before it.
- **Requirements**: counts per list value. See [Needs and run sheets](/docs/guide/needs-and-run-sheets).
- **Run sheets**: versions you can generate and send.
- **Payments**: payment requests for this order. See [Payments](/docs/guide/payments).
- **Messages**: the message the order was started from, and replies from the customer. See [The inbox](/docs/guide/inbox).
- **Export**: downloads the order as a json file for someone outside Bibi.

# Move it through your statuses

Your administrators decide the statuses, their names and their order under **Settings, Statuses**. Choose **Change status** on the order page, or drag the card on the **Pipeline** board.

What a status does is set with a few flags:

- **New orders start here**: the entry status.
- **Needs a reason**: you must say why, for example when an order is lost.
- **Needs an assignee**: the order must have an assignee first.
- **Ends the order**: nothing leaves it, and the order's rooms and resources are released.
- **Can be invoiced**: payments can still be requested.

Which moves are allowed from each status is also set by your administrators. If a move is refused, Bibi tells you every reason at once and nothing changes. Use **Change assignee** to set who answers for the order, and **Follow** to stay informed.

# Coming later

Line states (prebooked, booked, ordered) and signing by BankID are decided but not built yet.

inbox.title: The inbox and starting from a message
inbox.lead: Booking requests that come in by email, form or API wait in the inbox. From there you can start an order, with the assistant reading the request for you.
inbox.body:
# The inbox

Open **Inbox** to see requests that have no order yet: mail sent to your organization's address, requests a partner system or form handed in, and other channels as they are added. Each row shows the subject, the sender, the channel and when it arrived. Choose a message to read it. You can **Dismiss** a message you do not need (and **Restore** it from the Dismissed view) or **Attach** it to an order that already exists, where it joins the order's messages.

# Start an order from a message

Choose **Create order from this message**, or **Start from a message** at the top of the new order page and paste the text. The first step shows the request in a text area. Choose **Read the request** to let the assistant read it, or **Fill in by hand instead**.

The assistant fills the steps for you and opens the package step:

- **Who**: the customer and contact are filled when both match what you already have: the sender's email domain and the company name, and the contact's email. Otherwise the customer search starts with the company or the sender.
- **When and how many**: filled when the date, both times and the number of guests were read, otherwise prefilled with what was found.
- **Package**: a matching package is marked **Suggested from the email**.
- **Notes and needs**: the request and any needs, such as "Vegan x 2", start the booking note.

A panel, **What the assistant read**, lists every value with the quote from the message it came from, so you can check it. Values the assistant guessed, for example an end time the mail does not give, are marked **Guessed**. Each guess becomes an open question in the review, such as "The email doesn't say the end time. The assistant guessed 17:00." Choose **Keep** or change it.

# Nothing is created without you

Reading only fills in the form. Nothing is saved until you check the review and choose **Create order**, and then the message is attached to the new order and shows under its **Messages**. If the assistant cannot read the request, the page says so and you continue by hand. The text of a message comes from outside, so Bibi treats it as data: it never follows instructions written in it. Needs, packages and customers are matched against your own lists, never invented.

See [Orders](/docs/guide/orders) for the steps, the review and Create.

items-and-venues.title: Items and venues
items-and-venues.lead: Venues are your buildings and sites. Items are everything you sell or book: rooms, dishes, drinks, equipment and bundles.
items-and-venues.body:
# Venues

A venue is a building or site. Items belong to a venue.

1. Open **Venues** in the left menu and choose **Create venue**.
2. Enter the name, address, contact details and opening hours.
3. Save. The venue page lists the items at that venue.

Archiving a venue also archives its items.

# Items

An item is anything that can be sold or booked. What an item looks like depends on its **type**, and your administrators define the types. A "Conference room" type might have fields for floor and area. A "Dish" type might have a price and a list of allergens.

To add an item:

1. Open **Items** and choose **Create item**.
2. Pick the type, then fill in the name, description, venue and the type's fields.
3. Save.

If no types exist yet, choose **Go to types** and create one first. Use the type filter on the list to find items quickly.

# What a type can do

When a type is created it can switch on any of these capabilities. They are the only things Bibi builds in. Everything else is your own naming.

- **Priced**: the item has a price, a price unit (per person, per unit, per hour or flat) and VAT.
- **Bundle**: the item contains other items, with quantity and timing. A conference day is an example.
- **Customisations**: any item can offer groups of options, other items that are included, charged extra or replace its price, for example "choose 1 of 3 main courses".
- **Bookable**: the item can be occupied in time, and Bibi stops double booking. A room is an example.
- **Setups**: a bookable item has a capacity per setup, for example 80 people in Theatre and 40 in U-shape.

# Setups and changeover

Setups are your named room layouts, such as Cinema, U-shape or Mingle. Each has a changeover time, which Bibi blocks right before a line that uses it. Create them under **Settings, Setups**, and set the capacity per setup on each bookable item.

# Bundles for one customer

On a customer page, choose **Save as bundle** to build a bundle from catalog items. The bundle is shown only for that customer and the catalog does not change.

# Contents of an item

An item that contains other items shows **Contents** with what it **Contains** (mandatory parts) and what it **May contain** (optional parts and choices). This is what Bibi compares with the counts you record. See [Needs and run sheets](/docs/guide/needs-and-run-sheets).

# Blocking an item

To take a room out of use for maintenance or internal use, open the item and choose **Block item**. Bookings cannot overlap a block. Choose **Release block** to open it again.

# Prices for a customer

Price lists let you give a customer a general discount or special prices per item. See [Configuration](/docs/guide/configuration).

needs-and-run-sheets.title: Needs and run sheets
needs-and-run-sheets.lead: Record what an order needs as counts, and send versioned run sheets to the people who prepare it. No personal data about guests is stored.
needs-and-run-sheets.body:
# Needs are counts

A need (called a requirement in the app) is a number against a value in one of your own lists. For example, if your organization has a list of allergens, "Gluten x 3" means three guests need gluten-free food. "Wheelchair x 2" works the same way with an accessibility list.

Needs are never tied to a named person. You never enter a guest's name or health details.

# Add a need to an order

1. Open the order and go to **Requirements**.
2. Choose **Add requirement**.
3. Pick the list value and enter the count.
4. Choose where it applies: **Whole order**, or one line.

You can only have one count per list value in each place. If you try to add a second one you are asked to edit the existing count. A count on a line replaces the order's count for that item, value by value. A count of 0 on a line means "none here".

If your administrators gave the need type extra fields, such as severity, you can fill those in too. Use **Remove requirement** if a count is no longer needed.

# Matching against items

Bibi compares each need with the items on the order that carry the same list value. The result is shown as one of two kinds of match.

- **Contains**: the item, or a mandatory part of it, is tagged with that value.
- **May contain**: only optional parts or choice options carry it.

A match that **Contains** and has no alternative **blocks** the run sheet. The run sheet shows **Blocked: cannot be sent** until you fix the order, for example by picking an alternative.

# Run sheets

A run sheet is a compilation for one responsibility, for example a kitchen order for the head of kitchen. Your administrators define which run sheets exist, what each one includes and who receives it. See [Configuration](/docs/guide/configuration).

1. Open the order and go to **Run sheets**.
2. Choose **Generate version**. Bibi takes a snapshot of the order with what that run sheet includes.
3. Review the rows, the counts and any matches.
4. Choose **Send**.

# Versions and changes

Every time the order changes you can generate a new version. Bibi marks what was **Added**, **Changed** or **Removed since the last sent version**, so the kitchen sees what is new. A version is never edited or deleted, and each version can be sent once.

Run sheets can be sent while the order is open. Once it has reached a status that ends it, you can still read the run sheets but not send them. Only the latest version can be sent.

# Coming later

Exporting a run sheet as JSON, PDF or CSV for handover outside the system is planned but not available yet.

payments.title: Payments
payments.lead: Ask a customer to pay by card link or by invoice. The money goes straight to your own Stripe account, and Bibi never holds it.
payments.body:
# Connect Stripe first

Before you can request a payment, an administrator must connect your organization to Stripe.

1. Open **Settings** and choose **Integrations**.
2. Choose **Connect to Stripe**. You are sent to Stripe to verify your business.
3. When you come back, choose **Refresh status**. If onboarding is not finished, choose **Continue onboarding**.

The status shows **Not connected**, **Onboarding**, **Active** or **Restricted**. Payments work when it is **Active**. If it is **Restricted**, Stripe needs more information from you, so continue onboarding.

Payments are charged on your own connected account, so you are the merchant and the payout goes to you.

# Request a payment

1. Open the order and find **Payments**.
2. Choose **Request payment**.
3. Pick the method and the amount.
4. Save.

There are two methods.

- **Card**: Bibi creates a payment link. Choose **Open payment link** to copy or open it, and send it to the customer.
- **Invoice**: Stripe emails an invoice to the customer. The customer needs an email address on the customer record. The due date follows the customer's payment terms, 30 days if none is set.

You can request a payment for an open order, or for one in a closing status that can be invoiced.

# What the customer sees

The customer opens the link and lands on a simple page with your organization name, the booking reference, the amount and a **Pay now** button. Stripe handles the card details. The customer does not need an account and never sees Bibi's app.

If the link has expired, the page says so and asks the customer to contact you. You can then request a new payment.

# Payment status

Each payment has a status: **Pending**, **Paid**, **Failed**, **Cancelled** or **Refunded**. The status updates by itself when Stripe reports back. You do not need to mark anything as paid.

# Paid does not move the order

A paid payment only changes the payment's status. The order stays in its status, and you move it yourself when you are ready.

# Coming later

Swish for customers, price lists applied to invoices, and invoices sent to Fortnox, Visma or Peppol are decided but not available yet.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.lead: Admins set up what things are called and how they work in your organization. Everything here is your own data.
configuration.body:
# Who can configure

Only admins see **Settings** in the left menu. It opens a page that lists every configuration area. Changes affect everyone in the organization.

# Types and fields

Under **Settings, Types** you define the kinds of records you work with: items, customers, contacts, orders, requirements and lines. For example "Conference room", "Dish", "Company" or "Conference".

1. Choose **Create type**, say what it is for and name it.
2. For an item type, switch on capabilities such as **Priced**, **Bookable** or **Setups**. See [Items and venues](/docs/guide/items-and-venues).
3. Add fields. A field can be text, number, yes/no, date, choice, multiple choice or a link to another record. Mark it required if it must always be filled in.

A type cannot be archived while it is in use, and a field cannot change kind once it has data.

# Lists

Under **Settings, Lists** you keep your own word lists, such as allergens, diets or accessibility needs. Fields and needs point to a list. To get started, choose **Import the EU's 14 allergens**. You can edit the list afterwards. A list or a value cannot be archived while a field uses it or a need counts it.

# Setups

Under **Settings, Setups** you name your room layouts and set the changeover time. See [Items and venues](/docs/guide/items-and-venues).

# Statuses

Under **Settings, Statuses** you decide which statuses your orders move through, what they are called and in which order they appear on the pipeline board. Nothing about a status is fixed: each has a name, a colour and a few flags that decide what Bibi does. You need one entry status and at least one status that ends the order. See [Orders](/docs/guide/orders).

1. Choose **Create status**, or **Import conference venue template** for a ready set.
2. Orders can move from any status to any other. In the **Flow** section below the list, limit where a status may move to and set what a move into a status requires. Only admins see it.
3. Reorder with the arrows.

A status is archived, never deleted. If orders are in it, you choose the status they move to.

# Run sheets

Under **Settings, Run sheets** you define a run sheet such as "Kitchen order": name it, choose which item types and fields it includes, which lists' needs it counts, and which role receives it. See [Needs and run sheets](/docs/guide/needs-and-run-sheets).

# Price lists

Under **Settings, Price lists** you create a list for a customer or for everyone, with a validity period. Choose either a general discount in percent, or a price per item, not both. New order lines use the list's prices, and an archived list no longer applies.

# Payments and skills

**Settings, Payments** connects Stripe. See [Payments](/docs/guide/payments). **Settings, Skills** holds organization skills for the assistant. See [The assistant](/docs/guide/assistant).

# Templates and the assistant

Templates such as the conference venue starter set are optional. They are only data, so you can change everything afterwards. You can also ask the assistant to propose a setup, for example "We are a manor with a restaurant". You approve each change.

members-and-roles.title: Members and roles
members-and-roles.lead: Invite colleagues, give them the right access level and remove them when they leave.
members-and-roles.body:
# Access levels

Every member has one preset, which an admin can fine-tune per person. The presets are fixed and go from least to most access.

- **Member**: can read everything, and changes nothing.
- **Manager**: can also handle bookings and day-to-day data such as customers, orders, lines, needs, payments and run sheets.
- **Admin**: everything in the organization: configuration (types, lists, statuses, run sheets, price lists), members, API keys and the organization itself. An organization always keeps at least one admin.

# Fine-tune one person

An admin can give one person more or less than their preset, per part of the app.

1. Open **Settings** and choose **Members**.
2. On the person's row, choose **Permissions**.
3. Turn **Read**, **Write** or **Delete** on or off, for example let a member also write items, or hide payments from a manager. **Write** covers creating, changing, sending and exporting, and moving an order to another status. Turning off **Read** hides that part of the app for them.
4. Choose **Save**.

Changed cells are marked, and **Reset** puts them back to the preset. Managing members, API keys and the payment account always stays with admins.

You only see the parts of the app you may view. The pages check your access themselves, so hiding the menu is only a convenience.

# Invite a colleague

1. Open **Settings** and choose **Members**.
2. Choose **Invite member** and enter the email address and role.
3. Choose **Send invitation**.

Bibi emails a link. The person signs in or creates an account with that same email address and chooses **Accept invitation**. They then join with the invited role. An invitation expires after 48 hours.

Under **Pending invitations** you can see who has not answered yet. Choose **Revoke** to cancel an invitation, and the link stops working. You cannot give someone more access than you have yourself, and an email address that is already a member cannot be invited again.

# Change a role or remove someone

On the members page you can change a member's role. You cannot change or remove someone whose role is above your own. To remove someone, choose **Remove**. They lose access immediately, and what they created stays in the history.

# Who does what on an order

Access roles decide what you may do in the app. A separate idea decides who answers for an order.

- Every order has one assignee, who must be a member. Other members can follow it to stay informed.
- Some statuses need an assignee before an order can enter them, for example Confirmed.
- Change the assignee with **Change assignee**, and choose **Follow** or **Unfollow** for yourself. The order list can show only what is **Assigned to me** or what you are **Following**.

Administrators define responsibilities such as "Head of kitchen" under **Settings, Responsibilities**. A responsibility covers certain item types and has a default person and followers. Coming later: an order gets an assignee per responsibility automatically from its items, and the matching run sheets go to that person and the followers.

# The assistant and API access

The assistant acts with your permissions, so it can never do more than you can. Tools you connect with OAuth act as you too. API keys belong to the organization and have their own permissions, set by an admin. See [Authentication](/docs/developers/authentication).

overview.title: Developer overview
overview.lead: Bibi has four ways in: the web app, a REST API, a GraphQL graph and an MCP server. They all run the same operations with the same permissions.
overview.body:
# One set of operations, four surfaces

Every capability in Bibi is defined once as a **core operation**, for example `venue.create` or `order.list`. Each operation has an input schema, an output schema, a required permission and a handler. The surfaces are generated from that list:

- **REST** at `{{webUrl}}/api/v1`, described by an OpenAPI 3.1 document.
- **GraphQL** at `{{webUrl}}/api/graphql`, for reading related data in one request.
- **MCP** at `{{mcpUrl}}/mcp`, one tool per operation, for AI assistants such as Claude.
- **The web app**, which staff use every day.

Because everything comes from the same operations, a command that exists in the web app also exists in REST and MCP, with the same validation and the same errors. A parity test in CI keeps it that way.

# Tenancy

All data belongs to an **organization**. Every credential resolves to one user in one organization, and every operation is scoped to that organization. You can never read or change another organization's data, whichever surface you use.

# Audit and logging

Every command writes an audit log entry with the actor (`user` or `ai`), the surface and a request id. Organization admins can read the history in the app and through `auditLog.list`.

# Where to go next

- [Authentication](/docs/developers/authentication): API keys, sessions and OAuth.
- [REST API](/docs/developers/rest-api) and the [REST reference]({{webUrl}}/api/v1/docs).
- [MCP server](/docs/developers/mcp) and the [MCP tool reference](/docs/reference/mcp).
- [AI approvals](/docs/developers/approvals): why AI commands become proposals.
- [Errors and limits](/docs/developers/errors).

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.lead: Every request is made as a user in one organization. Use an API key for server-to-server integrations and OAuth for MCP clients and third-party apps.
authentication.body:
# API keys (REST and GraphQL)

An API key belongs to the organization, not to a person. It has a preset (member, manager or admin), which an admin can fine-tune on the key's **Permissions** page. Send it as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer bib_<your key>
```

The `x-api-key: bib_<your key>` header works too. Keys always start with `bib_`.

- Keys are rate limited to 600 requests per minute.
- The key keeps working when the admin who created it leaves. Revoke it in **Settings** when it is no longer needed.
- Treat a key like a password. Never put it in front-end code or a public repository.

Only admins create, change and revoke API keys, under **Settings, Integrations**.

# OAuth 2.1 (MCP clients and apps)

MCP clients such as Claude Desktop sign in with OAuth. The client is sent to the Bibi sign-in page, the user signs in and picks an organization, and the client receives an access token that acts as that user.

- Discovery: `{{webUrl}}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`
- Protected resource metadata for MCP: `{{mcpUrl}}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`
- Authorization endpoint: `{{webUrl}}/api/auth/oauth2/authorize`
- Token endpoint: `{{webUrl}}/api/auth/oauth2/token`
- Scopes: `bibi:read` and `bibi:write`

Most MCP clients do all of this for you when you add the server URL.

# Session cookie

The web app uses a session cookie. Requests from a signed-in browser to `/api/v1` and `/api/graphql` are authenticated the same way. This is meant for the app itself, not for integrations.

# Permissions

Each member has one of three fixed roles: **member**, **manager** or **admin**. Every operation names the permission it needs, for example `venue:create`. The reference lists the permission for each route and tool. A call without it fails with `FORBIDDEN`.

rest-api.title: REST API
rest-api.lead: A JSON API under /api/v1 with one route per operation, described by an OpenAPI 3.1 document that is generated from the code.
rest-api.body:
# Base URL and spec

- Base URL: `{{webUrl}}/api/v1`
- OpenAPI document: [{{webUrl}}/api/v1/openapi.json]({{webUrl}}/api/v1/openapi.json)
- Interactive reference (browse every route and try requests): [{{webUrl}}/api/v1/docs]({{webUrl}}/api/v1/docs)

You can generate a typed client from the OpenAPI document with any OpenAPI generator.

# Requests

- Reads use `GET`. Query parameters carry filters and pagination.
- Creates use `POST`, updates use `PATCH`, archives and removals use `DELETE` or a `POST` to an action route.
- Bodies are JSON. Send `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Dates and times are ISO 8601 strings in UTC, for example `2026-11-05T09:00:00.000Z`.

```
curl "{{webUrl}}/api/v1/venues?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer bib_<your key>"
```

# Pagination

List routes take `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) and `cursor`. The response has `items` and `nextCursor`. Pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` to get the next page. When `nextCursor` is `null` you have reached the end.

```
{ "items": [ ... ], "nextCursor": "clx2..." }
```

# Configurable fields

Organizations define their own types, fields and lists. Entities that support it carry a `fields` object with the organization's custom values. Read the organization's field definitions (`GET /field-definitions`) to know which keys and value types to expect.

# Responses and errors

Success returns `200` (or `201` for creates) with the operation's output as JSON. Failures return the error envelope described in [Errors and limits](/docs/developers/errors).

graphql.title: GraphQL
graphql.lead: A read-focused graph for fetching related data in one request, for example an order with its program, needs and run sheets.
graphql.body:
# Endpoint

`POST {{webUrl}}/api/graphql` with a JSON body of `query`, `variables` and optionally `operationName`. Authenticate the same way as REST (API key, OAuth token or session).

```
curl -X POST "{{webUrl}}/api/graphql" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer bib_<your key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"{ venues { items { id name } } }"}'
```

# Schema

The schema is generated from the same operations and Zod schemas as REST and MCP. Every entity can be read through the graph, and every command is also available as a mutation.

Introspection is turned off in production. Get the schema as SDL from the MCP tool `graphql_schema`, or run the app locally where GraphiQL and introspection are on.

# Limits

Queries are checked for depth and cost before they run. A query that is too deep or too expensive is rejected with a validation error. Split it into smaller queries or use pagination.

# When to use GraphQL or REST

- Use **GraphQL** to read a tree of related data in one round trip.
- Use **REST** for simple integrations, webhooks-style syncs and anything where an OpenAPI client is convenient.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.lead: Connect Claude or any other MCP client to Bibi. The assistant works as you, with your permissions, and every change waits for your approval.
mcp.body:
# Server URL

`{{mcpUrl}}/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). The server is stateless: each request is authenticated with an OAuth access token.

# Connect a client

1. In your MCP client (for example Claude Desktop or Claude Code), add a remote MCP server with the URL above.
2. The client opens the Bibi sign-in page. Sign in and choose the organization.
3. The client receives a token and lists the tools. You are ready.

The client discovers the authorization server through `{{mcpUrl}}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, so there is nothing else to configure.

# Tools

There is one tool per core operation. The name is the operation name with dots replaced by underscores: `venue.create` becomes `venue_create`. Each tool has a JSON Schema for its input and output, and hints that tell the client whether it is read-only or changes data. See the full [MCP tool reference](/docs/reference/mcp).

Two generic tools make reading easier:

- `graphql_schema` returns the GraphQL schema as SDL.
- `graphql_query` runs a read-only GraphQL query. Mutations are rejected.

The assistant also gets the organization's own field and type names in the tool descriptions, so it can use the words your venue uses.

# Changes need approval

When an AI assistant calls a tool that changes data, Bibi does **not** run it. It answers with `status: approval_required` and a short summary. The user approves or cancels the proposal in the Bibi app. Read [AI approvals](/docs/developers/approvals) for the details.

# Untrusted content

Some tools return text that came from outside the organization, for example received e-mails. These tools are marked as untrusted output, so clients and the assistant treat the content as data, never as instructions.

approvals.title: AI approvals
approvals.lead: AI proposes, people decide. Commands called by an AI actor are turned into proposals that a person must approve in the app.
approvals.body:
# How it works

1. The assistant calls a command, for example `order_create`.
2. Instead of running it, the MCP server returns a proposal:

```
{
  "status": "approval_required",
  "operation": "order.create",
  "summary": "Create order Board meeting on 5 Nov for Acme AB",
  "approvalToken": "...",
  "expiresAt": "2026-11-04T10:10:00.000Z"
}
```

3. The app shows the proposal as a card. The user reads the summary and clicks **Approve** or **Cancel**.
4. On approval, the app runs the command as the user. The audit log records `actor=ai`, the conversation and who approved it.

Proposals expire after 10 minutes. The assistant must not retry a command that is waiting for approval.

# What needs approval

- Every command (anything that changes data) called by an AI actor needs approval by default.
- Queries (reads) never need approval.
- The reference marks each route and tool that needs approval with a badge.

# Integrations with API keys

Calls made with an API key or by a person in the app are not AI calls. They run directly, with the permissions of the key or the user. Approval is only for AI actors.

errors.title: Errors and limits
errors.lead: Every surface returns the same typed errors, with a stable code, a message and field-level issues.
errors.body:
# Error envelope

REST returns errors as JSON with a matching HTTP status:

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION",
    "message": "Invalid input",
    "issues": [ { "path": "name", "message": "Required" } ]
  }
}
```

`issues[].path` is the field, dot-joined for nested fields (`rooms.0.name`). MCP tools return the same object with `isError: true`. GraphQL puts the code in `errors[].extensions.code`.

# Codes

- `VALIDATION` (400): the input did not match the schema. Check `issues`.
- `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401): no credential or an invalid one.
- `FORBIDDEN` (403): signed in, but the role lacks the permission or you are not a member of the organization.
- `NOT_FOUND` (404): the record does not exist in your organization.
- `CONFLICT` (409): the change clashes with existing data, for example an overlapping occupancy or a duplicate name.
- `UNAVAILABLE` (503): a capability is not set up right now, for example no AI model is configured.
- `INTERNAL` (500): something went wrong on our side. Retry later and quote the request id if you contact support.

# Limits

- API keys: 600 requests per minute.
- List pages: at most 100 items per request.
- GraphQL: queries have a maximum depth and cost.
- MCP `graphql_query`: queries only, with a maximum length.

# Retries

Reads are safe to retry. For commands, check the result before retrying a request that timed out, so you do not create the same record twice.
